title: Same-frame ESC + popover/QoS click: mapping-time UI side effects execute before the queued Cancel — old code deselected synchronously first
location: app/input/mouse.odin (mouse_map phase-1 keys + press branch) / app/main.odin (effect_ui_press, popover_click)
detail: Cancel is only queued for the executor, but on_ui_press→popover_click/qos_panel_click mutates topology synchronously during mapping. ESC + demolish-button click same frame: old code cleared the selection first (click no-op'd); new code demolishes, then deselects.
recommended_fix: Route popover/QoS commands through intents (Demolish/Set_Lane) so executor ordering applies, or run the UI press hit-test after the frame's queued phase-1 cancels have executed.

title: ESC + release while placing: stale drag.active routes to Drag_Release, whose click-select never re-checks the swallow latch (Select does)
location: app/input/mouse.odin (release else-if chain) / app/input/exec.odin (apply_intent Drag_Release case)
evidence:
+	} else if has_release || moves_n > 0 {
+		if inp.drag.active && placing_eff < 0 {
...
+			if has_release {
+				wx, wy := rnd.from_screen(inp.view, release_pos.x, release_pos.y)
+				append(out, Intent(Cursor_Move{wx = wx, wy = wy}))
+				append(out, Intent(Drag_Release{pos = release_pos}))
...
+	case Drag_Release:
+		commit_draw(inp)
+		mouse := v.pos
+		moved := rl.Vector2Distance(mouse, inp.press) > 6
+		if !moved && !release_ui_hit(inp, mouse) {
+			click_select(inp, mouse)
+		}
...contradicting Cancel's own contract:...
+		// placing). The swallow latch is always set — the cancel gesture's
+		// release must not re-select.
detail: The placement ghost sets drag.active (exec Cursor_Move), so on an ESC+release frame the mapping branches on pre-Cancel state and emits Drag_Release; its click-select path ignores press_swallowed. The cancel gesture's release now re-selects — the old synchronous cancel made that branch unreachable.
recommended_fix: Re-check placing/drag/press_swallowed at execution time inside Drag_Release (as Select and Demolish already do), or have the mapping suppress release intents when esc_cancelled is set.

title: Chord Press_Anchor runs after Right_Click and clears the drag-interrupt latch the old code left set
detail: Old net latch after a chord interrupting a drag: true (interrupt ran last). New: Right_Click sets it, then unconditional Press_Anchor clears it. With pad-Confirm/touch drags (drag.active with no button held), the chord's left release now click-selects, violating the stated invariant.
recommended_fix: Emit Press_Anchor only when a same-frame Cancel was actually emitted, or order the anchor reset before Right_Click so the drag-interrupt latch survives.

title: Game_Over R+Enter same frame emits two Retry intents — the comment claims || coalescing; restart_run fires twice
detail: poll_mouse can emit both R and Enter Key_Press events in one frame; each becomes a Retry, so effect_retry→restart_run runs twice (double destroy/re-init, two fresh seeds). Cross-device R + pad A doubles too. Old code restarted exactly once.
recommended_fix: Coalesce Retry like P/Space: emit at most one Retry per frame from the Game_Over block (a local flag), or dedupe Retry in the executor.

title: Class keys hard-capped at 1/2: the retained generic loop can never match i>=2; old code polled ONE+i per packet type
detail: The Key enum + poll stop at Two, so loop iterations for i>=2 are dead comparisons; if the catalog grows a third packet type its class key silently stops working (old code derived keys from len(packet_types)). The 'roster is exactly the current handle_input keys' claim only holds for exactly two classes.
recommended_fix: Either bound the loop at 2 with an explicit comment, or extend the Key enum/poll roster to cover the catalog's class count.

title: mouse_map silently drops Mouse_Move events beyond its fixed buffer of 2 — harness-scripted frames can truncate a drag path without signal
evidence:
+	// W5 (Perkins): no per-frame heap churn — the poll emits at most ONE
+	// Mouse_Move per frame, so a fixed buffer suffices (the project-context
+	// zero-per-frame-heap-churn rule).
+	moves: [2]rl.Vector2
+	moves_n := 0
...
+		case Mouse_Move:
+			if moves_n < len(moves) {
+				moves[moves_n] = e.pos
+				moves_n += 1
+			}
detail: The size-2 justification covers only the live poll (one move per frame), but the harness parity test scripts synthetic frames directly; a scripted frame with >2 moves silently loses re-snaps — a parity-test blind spot with no error, no assertion, no log.
recommended_fix: Assert or log on moves buffer overflow (or size it to the harness's documented maximum) so dropped moves are loud rather than silent.

title: Self-referential rename note: '(Cmd_Set_Weights -> Cmd_Set_Weights)' documents a no-op rename
evidence:
+// (set_lane_key + the lane command producers moved into app/input/exec.odin
+// in story 5.4 — the 1/2 + E/S/B keys now route through the intent layer's
+// shared executor; the #55 terminology rename (Cmd_Set_Weights ->
+// Cmd_Set_Weights) is reflected there.)
detail: The rename's source and target are identical — the comment is stale or mis-copied (presumably the pre-#55 command name). It misleads future readers about what was actually renamed.
recommended_fix: Correct the comment to name the actual pre-rename command, or drop the parenthetical entirely.
